benefits: Personal stipend of EUR 3,500 per month, paid directly to the fellow, which NIAS states should cover essential expenses during the fellowship
For researchers affiliated with a Dutch university or research institute who continue to receive their salary, a Dutch University Grant of EUR 3,500 per month paid to the institution instead
Five or ten months of research time at NIAS in Amsterdam, with an office at NIAS, laptop, telephone, research facilities and library services
Subsidised accommodation in Amsterdam where eligible, or reimbursement of local public transport
Travel expense reimbursement for fellows from outside the Netherlands, and commuting reimbursement for fellows living in the Netherlands
Participation in the academic, community and outreach programme, the weekly fellows' seminar, and the opportunity to meet Dutch academics, policymakers and representatives of financial institutions
eligibility: For researchers and policymakers in applied monetary economics, macroeconomics or public finance, at least three years after their PhD; applicants must have that experience by the closing date of the call

Open to researchers and policymakers from the Netherlands or abroad; primarily established mid- to late-career, with exceptionally talented early-career researchers also encouraged to apply, and a permanent position at a university or research institute is not required
Applicants should speak and write English well enough to take a full part in the life of the institute and to benefit from the responses of their peers
A fellowship at NIAS is a full-time commitment; fellows are expected to be at the institute four days a week from the start to the end of their fellowship, including the weekly fellows' seminar
Applicants may apply only once per call, and may not apply while another of their applications is under review at NIAS

In line with EU sanctions introduced in March 2022, NIAS cannot accept applications from researchers of any nationality affiliated with universities or research institutes in Russia or Belarus; researchers of Russian or Belarusian nationality who are independent or affiliated with an institution outside Russia or Belarus are eligible
requirements: Applications are submitted through the online application form during the published call window
A project proposal of no more than 1,500 words, including footnotes and excluding references
The proposal must contain at least a research question, a clear description of the project to be carried out at NIAS, and the methodological and theoretical contribution it aims to make
The proposal must be embedded in the existing literature and include a short list of references
Be present at NIAS four days a week for the duration of the fellowship
documents: Project proposal of no more than 1,500 words, including footnotes and excluding references, embedded in the existing literature with a short list of references
Up-to-date CV of no more than three pages, opening with a narrative section of no more than 300 words and listing up to ten key publications
Names of three international experts who could act as referees, without conflicts of interest
selection_criteria: The Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship Foundation gives priority to researchers with an outstanding record in applied monetary economics, macroeconomics or public finance
The Open Call is project-based: NIAS awards fellowships first and foremost on the quality of the research proposal, with the applicant's CV and publication record weighing less heavily
A NIAS staff committee proposes up to 150 applicants for peer review by external referees; the Fellowship Advisory Committee and the Director then take the decision
The two questions on interdisciplinary added value and contribution to the NIAS community are assessed in the second stage and carry real weight in the selection
One fellowship is awarded per academic year
coverage: Personal stipend of EUR 3,500 per month, paid directly to the fellow, which NIAS states should cover essential expenses during the fellowship
Dutch University Grant of EUR 3,500 per month paid to the institution for fellows affiliated to a Dutch university or research institute who continue to receive their salary

An office at NIAS with a laptop and telephone, access to research facilities and library services, and subsidised accommodation in Amsterdam where eligible (fellow contributes EUR 975 per month, NIAS contributes EUR 1,350 per month)

An international return ticket for fellows from outside the Netherlands: an allowance equivalent to one return train ticket within Europe below 500 km (max EUR 0.25 per kilometre), one return flight ticket (max EUR 500) in Europe at 500 km or more, and one return flight ticket (max EUR 1,500) from outside Europe

Reimbursement of daily commuting travel expenses for fellows living in the Netherlands within 90 minutes one-way of NIAS, up to EUR 250 per month, plus one second-class return ticket by public transport for fellows who have been granted accommodation

Complete all five sections of the form: type of fellowship, personal details, work and career, practical information, and the project proposal
Upload the project proposal and CV in PDF, DOC or DOCX format
Enter the names of three international experts without conflicts of interest, and answer the two questions on interdisciplinary and community engagement
Check for the automatic acknowledgement of receipt sent to the work email address given in the form
official.application_route: Apply online through the NIAS application form during the annual open call window (15 January to 15 March), submitting the completed form, the project proposal and the CV.
official.study_mode: Full-time; a fellowship at NIAS is a residency in the full sense of the word
official.citizenship_residency: Open to researchers and policymakers from the Netherlands or abroad; no nationality restriction beyond the EU sanctions rule on affiliation with institutions in Russia or Belarus
official.international_eligibility: Yes: the fellowship is open to researchers from the Netherlands and abroad, and NIAS supports fellows from outside the Netherlands with travel and accommodation arrangements
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applied monetary economics, macroeconomics, macroeconomic policy, public finance or public finance policy; the Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship Foundation, supported by De Nederlandsche Bank, the Dutch Ministry of Finance, ING Group, Rabobank, ABN AMRO and AEGON, gives priority to researchers with an outstanding record in these fields
official.research_requirement: A project proposal of no more than 1,500 words including footnotes and excluding references, describing the research to be carried out at NIAS, with a research question, relation to existing literature, methodological and theoretical contribution, time schedule and intended results
official.duration: Five or ten months, as either a five-month or a ten-month semester
official.description: The Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship is for researchers and policymakers in applied monetary economics, macroeconomics and public finance. It allows fellows to pursue their own work within the international and multidisciplinary community at NIAS in Amsterdam, with the opportunity to meet Dutch academics, policymakers and representatives of financial institutions.
official.region: Netherlands (Amsterdam); NIAS is an institute of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences
official.program_type: Individual research fellowship (residency) at NIAS, funded by the Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship Foundation
official.english_requirement: Applicants should have a good command of English, the working language at NIAS, and speak and write it well enough to take a full part in the life of the institute and to benefit from the responses of their peers; no IELTS or TOEFL score is published

applicant_utility.summary: One five- or ten-month residency in Amsterdam is offered each academic year, and the money is a flat monthly stipend rather than a tuition package, so think of it as salary replacement plus an Amsterdam housing problem you have to solve. The proposal, not the publication list, is what the referees actually grade, and the call closes at noon CET on 15 March 2027, which is a hard cut-off. If you are employed by a Dutch university you can keep your salary and have the EUR 3,500 per month paid to your institution instead, but your dean has to agree to the terms first.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A mid-career economist in monetary economics, macroeconomics or public finance with at least three years post-PhD, a publication record and a project that can realistically be finished in five or ten months of uninterrupted writing in Amsterdam.
application_readiness_checklist: Draft the proposal to answer the three questions referees will ask: what is the research question, what literature does it sit in, and what will be finished by the end of the stay
Count words the way NIAS does: 1,500 including footnotes, references excluded, and a reference list that is clearly a list of references
Rebuild the CV to fit three pages with a 300-word narrative opening and a maximum of ten key publications, since over-length dossiers are rejected automatically
Line up three referees with no conflict of interest before the window opens and confirm each of them is willing to be approached
Write both community questions as seriously as the proposal; they are scored in the second stage and often decide between comparable projects

If you are at a Dutch institution, brief your head of department or dean before submitting, because their agreement is required for the Dutch University Grant route; then submit in the first weeks of January rather than on the closing day
common_rejection_risks: Proposal above the 1,500-word limit or without a reference list, which makes the application formally ineligible regardless of quality
A research agenda rather than a project: no time schedule and no statement of what the residency will produce
Referees who are co-authors, former supervisors or same-department colleagues, which reads as a conflict of interest
Thin answers to the two community questions, which the staff committee weighs in the second-stage screening
Missing the noon CET closing time on 15 March 2027, or submitting while another NIAS application of yours is still under review
Having held a NIAS fellowship less than ten years before the closing date, or being affiliated with an institution in Russia or Belarus
Applying while another NIAS application of yours is still under review, or submitting twice in the same call
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The EUR 975 per month you pay towards NIAS accommodation, health and liability insurance for the whole stay if you come from outside the Netherlands (a NIAS fellowship is not employment and carries no Dutch social-security cover), your share of any private rental above the EUR 1,350 monthly housing subsidy, excess baggage and travel insurance which are not reimbursed, parking, family travel, and daily living costs beyond what the stipend covers.
document_audit: Uploads must be PDF, DOC or DOCX; have both formats ready in case one corrupts
Footnotes count towards the 1,500 proposal words, so move background into references instead
The CV limit is three pages in total including the publication list, not three pages plus a publication list
The acknowledgement email goes to the work address you typed into the form, so check that inbox and its spam folder after submitting
Former NIAS fellows must be able to document the ten-year gap if asked
alerts: NIAS assesses a maximum of 216 eligible applications per open call, split into three affiliation categories of no more than 72, and announces a full category on the fellowship page, so late applicants in a full category are turned away
The fellowship is a full-time residency: four days a week at the institute, full-time presence during the first two weeks of the semester, and the Thursday afternoon fellows' seminar
Selection takes most of the year; NIAS states all eligible applicants hear the outcome by 15 December 2027 and the new cohort is announced in June 2028
Applicants with an incomplete or non-compliant application are notified by email by 1 May, which is the signal that the file was rejected on formal grounds rather than assessed
Incomplete or incorrect applications are rejected automatically, and NIAS reserves the right to extend invitations independently of the regular procedure
English is the working language of the institute; no test score is published, but the community sessions and weekly seminars are conducted entirely in English
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Fill in the NIAS online form in one sitting with the proposal, CV and three referee names already prepared, upload the files, then wait for the automatic acknowledgement email before assuming the file went through.
